subject.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB/TEXT type mismatches during STRICT migration

question: Should the migration automatically coerce every legacy BLOB value in canonical TEXT columns, or should it preflight and stop with actionable recovery when coercion could alter text semantics or collide with an existing canonical key?
rationale: The patch changes persisted-data normalization during an upgrade; source fixtures cover ordinary values but do not establish the intended policy for ambiguous binary values or normalized-key collisions.

options.title: Require conversion-safety proof
options.body: Add representative collision and non-text-byte coverage plus a direct upgrade run before accepting automatic coercion.

options.title: Fail with guided recovery
options.body: Keep the migration transactional and provide an actionable Doctor recovery path when conversion cannot be proven safe.

options.title: Accept automatic coercion
options.body: Treat all values in canonical TEXT columns as text-compatible and accept the residual legacy-data risk.

recommendation.title: Require conversion-safety proof
recommendation.body: Add representative collision and non-text-byte coverage plus a direct upgrade run before accepting automatic coercion.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the merged STRICT migration implementation and is the strongest available history-based routing candidate.
